Subject: Dedicated capacity: post-call recap + next steps

Sam \u2014 great to meet earlier. Quick recap from today's discovery and the integration/architecture items we agreed to follow up on: 

- Primary goals: predictable latency (95th <= 250ms for text-gen path), support for high-concurrency bursty workloads during market open (peak ~450 QPS), and on-prem-sensitive data handling (VPC + dedicated capacity).
- Integration points we discussed: SDK setup and auth (we'll use API keys + optional mTLS for private deployment), routing policies (latency-first in us-east, failover to us-west), and structured output/tool-calling for your alert enrichment pipeline.
- Embeddings/reranking: you plan to index ~150M docs and expect ~120 qps embedding lookups for reranking; we recommended vector DB with local caching and periodic batch re-embeds.
- Autoscaling and throughput sizing: rough starting baseline we discussed: a dedicated pool sized for sustained 120 QPS with burst capacity to 450 QPS using queue-based smoothing and short-lived scale-ups. We flagged concurrency limits per GPU and suggested request queueing with settable max backlog.

Action items (next steps):
1) I attached a MAP proposal with a draft sizing and ops runbook (FinEdge-REDWOOD-MAP-dedicated-capacity-proposal.pdf). Please review.
2) Sam \u2014 can you send a 24hr sample of traffic (anonymized) and a quick table of expected P95 latency SLOs per endpoint? You can drop the sample as request-traffic-sample.json or share a signed S3 link.
3) Aditya \u2014 can you propose concrete autoscaling and queue sizing parameters (initial CPU/GPU pool sizes, min/max instance counts, enqueue/dequeue thresholds, per-request concurrency limits) so we can align on SLA cost tradeoffs?
4) Let's schedule a follow-up with Eng & Infra to walk through the SDK auth flow and a short demo of structured output/tool-calls. 

Thanks \u2014 looking forward to the next sync.

— Marissa

Thanks \u2014 copied the traffic sample and MAP. High-level technical proposal for autoscaling/throughput/concurrency + queues based on the signals you provided: 

Summary (recommendation):
- Baseline pool: 6 GPUs (A100-equivalent) sized for sustained ~120 QPS (consider model variant quantization to reduce token cost).
- Burst capacity: autoscale up to 20 GPUs for handling peak 450 QPS bursts with warm-starting policy (keep a small warm buffer to avoid cold-start latency).
- Concurrency limits: cap per-GPU concurrent requests at ~8 concurrent generation streams for your expected request size (token length median 48). This yields ~48 concurrent streams per 6-GPU baseline.
- Queueing: adopt two priority queues \u2014 high (trading alerts) and standard. Queueing policy: if queue backlog > 500 requests for >30s, trigger scale-up; if high-priority queue backlog > 50 for >10s, force-provision additional warm GPUs or route to a pre-provisioned reserve pool. Soft-drop policy: drop only when total backlog > 10k and only for standard queue.
- Autoscaling signals: use combined signals (GPU utilization, QPS, queue-backlog, and request latency p95 crossing 80% of SLO). This avoids oscillation on a single metric.
- Cost mitigations: recommend prefix caching for repeated prompts and local embedding cache for top-K rerank to reduce embedding QPS.

Concrete params to start (we can tune after pilot):
- min_pool: 4 GPUs
- initial_pool: 6 GPUs
- max_pool: 20 GPUs
- per_gpu_concurrency_limit: 8
- high_queue_threshold_scale: backlog_high > 50 for 10s
- global_backlog_scale_threshold: backlog_total > 500 for 30s
- soft_drop_threshold: backlog_total > 10000

Auth pattern for Private: we recommend short-lived API keys minted by your KMS (STS-style), plus mTLS on the network boundary. For Hosted/Dedicated hybrid scenarios, we can support per-route API keys and signed JWTs. I can put an ops doc together with example SDK calls for mTLS + short-lived token exchange.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa/FinEdge: confirm initial params and whether you'd like a higher warm buffer (reserve pool) during market open.
- FinEdge: provide the signed 24h traffic or confirm we can pull from a shared S3 link for pilot.
- Redwood: we'll prepare a short runbook and a demo of the SDK auth flow + a draft of the autoscaling policy in the Console for the follow-up call on Thu 2/18 11am ET.
